Downloads: every ranged answer is checked, a file with a wrong SHA-256 is repaired piece by piece instead of deleted

A 39.8 GB shard came out with the wrong SHA-256 on 0.2.1 and was deleted, 40 GB of download lost.

- every ranged answer must be a 206 with exactly the Content-Range asked for (start, end and total), a fitting
  Content-Length and the same ETag as the first answer; a changed file part-way stops the download and drops the .part
- the raw unbuffered write is looped until every byte is down (its return value was ignored)
- a .part records the address and ETag it came from (.part.src); one from another mirror or revision is dropped, not mixed
- a parallel download always has a piece list before the first byte is written; if none can be kept it uses one stream,
  so holes in the sparse file are never read as a finished prefix
- the one-stream resume accepts a 206 only at the byte asked for; another range restarts from zero
- a finished file with a pinned hash but no finish mark is checked, not marked; the rename waits for a virus scanner
- a SHA-256 mismatch re-reads the file from the server piece by piece, rewrites only the blocks that differ and checks
  again ("Some parts of the file were damaged; downloading only those parts again"); deleted only if still wrong
- update archives (strata_control/transfer.py): a resumed answer is appended only when its Content-Range starts at the byte asked for
- tests: tests/terminal/test_download_integrity.py (a local server that answers 200 for ranges, wrong ranges and totals,
  cut bodies, another ETag, 503s, flipped bytes)

CPU pool: say where the workers run, --pool-cores (experimental), names for the engine's threads

The start-up now has one plain line: CPU workers on logical processors 2,4,...,30 (15 workers, one per physical core; host on 0).
It says so when two workers share a core, when the host's core is taken, and when the OS did not say which processors are
siblings. --pool-cores LIST / STRATA_POOL_CORES pins the workers to exactly the listed logical processors (off by default;
siblings, the host's processor and processors the process may not use are warned about, never refused). The default placement
is unchanged. The pool workers, the host thread and the long-lived helper threads get names (strata-pool-N, strata-host,
strata-stage, strata-adapt, ...), so ps -L, /proc and Windows thread tools show which is which. Windows without core
information no longer counts every logical processor as a core when it picks the default worker count.

Gyro decode (CUDA): trellis codebook in shared memory, 8-lane rows for the 160-dot gate/up and the 40-dot down

The int8 codebook lookups of tq_load went through the global table: a warp's 32 random 2-byte reads touched ~20 L1 sectors each
(native_expert_bench, ncu: 51M sectors for 2.8M requests, L1 64% busy). The grouped gate/up and down kernels now stage the 4 KB
codebook per block (stage_iq_grid, STRATA_IQ_STAGE_GRID=0 reads it in place) and take 4 rows per warp: gate/up K=160 (new
row_dot_160_sub8) and the K=40 down (row_dot_40_sub8, as IQ4_NL), 32 rows per block so the staging is amortised and no lane idles.
The sums keep row_dot_multi's tree (lane sums of t, t+8, t+16, t+24, then the same xor steps), so the outputs are bit for bit the
old ones: native_expert_bench prints an FNV hash of the outputs now, equal for base and new on Gyro-S, Gyro-M and Q2_0 blobs.

prefill: a padded activation is gfx11 only, and Gemm::native copies it unpadded instead of ending the engine

STRATA_PF_PAD=1 STRATA_PF_GEMM=1 lets the two K 6144 producers write row stride 6,208 into the prompt GEMM, but the only
product that reads a padded stride is strata_pf_gemm_f16_ld, which is built into wmma_gemm.cu's gfx11 matrix-core block
and returns false everywhere else.  On an RDNA4 card Gemm::native then reached its "a padded X (ldx 6208, K 6144) needs
STRATA_PF_PAD's path" branch and called std::exit(1): under serve/ that is one engine restart per request.  Reproduced
on an RX 9070 (gfx1201, ROCm 7.2.4, kernel 7.2.11) at --vram-reserve-mib 700 and 1,536, so it was not the VRAM guard.

- wmma_gemm.cu/.h: strata_pf_padded_gemm_available() answers whether the padded product exists on the current device
  (the same gfx11 list the kernels are compiled for; false in a build with no gfx11 target).
- prefill.cpp: pf_pad() asks it before padding, and prints one line when the env asks for a product this card has not.
- gemm.cu/.hpp: a padded X that no kernel took is copied to a contiguous FP16 buffer (one cudaMemcpy2DAsync, one
  grow-only buffer per Gemm) and the ordinary paths run - the same products, the same bits.  exit(1) remains only for a
  failed allocation, with a message that says so.

Checked on the RX 9070, same 1,199-token prompt and 8 greedy tokens in every arm:
- before (0.1.45, pre-fix binary): `prefill gemm: a padded X (ldx 6208, K 6144) needs STRATA_PF_PAD's path`, exit 1.
- after, STRATA_PF_PAD=1 STRATA_PF_GEMM=1: `prefill gemm: STRATA_PF_PAD needs the padded gfx11 product, which this card
  does not run; not padding`, prompt and decode complete, exit 0, output identical to the unpadded run.
- after, with the gate forced open so that the producers really pad and Gemm::native takes the copy path: no exit, no
  "needs STRATA_PF_PAD's path", output identical to the unpadded run (13 271 248046 198 248045 74455 198 248068).
  With the gate in place STRATA_PF_GEMM=1 alone is inert on this card (4K 1,247 against 1,243 tok/s, 8K 1,330 against
  1,321, medians of 3 starts).

Linux integrated GPU: the auto expert cache counts the RAM once (cache <= RAM available - desktop reserve); the APU warning uses the same reserve

A Strix Halo's free VRAM is the GPU pool (carve-out + GTT, nearly all RAM with ttm.pages_limit raised) while the cache copies experts into that
same RAM on top of the arena, so a cache sized from the pool alone could ask for more than the OS had left (OOM killer). The auto size is now
min(GPU free, MemAvailable - max(8 GiB, 8% of RAM)); --expert-cache N is kept as asked, STRATA_UMA_RESERVE_GIB=N sets the reserve (0 = old sizing).

Fix #3441, #3075: a drifted tool-call opener is read as the call; a call for a tool the request did not declare stays text

A <tool_call> whose opener drops the word function (<=NAME>, <function:NAME>, <NAME>) is read as <function=NAME> when NAME is a declared tool.
The answer follows the rule the reasoning already had (#804): a call counts only for a declared tool. Chat Completions and /v1/messages requests that declared no tools get the text back; the Responses route keeps its Codex compaction behaviour.
Blocks that open like a call but do not read as one are counted in the server window.

Fix #3503: the Linux cuda12 engine package carries sm_60/61/70; the source Dockerfile builds it

packaging/build_cuda_linux.sh is the recipe for the Linux cuda13 and cuda12 packages (cuda12: CUDA 12.9, 60;61;70;75;80;86;89, STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON, driver 575.51). package_engine.py refuses a cuda12 package without sm_60, sm_61 or sm_70, so the 0.2.1 mistake (sm_75/86/89 only, a P100 container in a restart loop) cannot ship again.

Fix #3480: the HIP queue priming stands aside when GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES is 1 or 2

With the runtime capped to two hardware queues the two primed queues are all of them, and the high-priority draft stream and the draft side stream share them: a 4K prompt on an RX 9060 XT read 681-753 tok/s primed and 1188-1238 unprimed. Fix #3465: after non-finite logits in a prompt window the retry reads the whole prompt batched

The reporter's prompts ended in non-finite logits in the window that reads the prompt's last few tokens (after the last turn boundary), every time and on every retry, and passed with --short-read 0. The cause on their machine (a Windows VM, sm_89, a Broadwell AVX2 CPU, IQ3_S) was not reproduced on a P100 with a Broadwell Xeon, an RTX 3060 or a Core Ultra.
The engine now reads the request that follows such a window with --short-read 0 for that one request, so the server's transparent retry succeeds instead of failing the same way. Nothing changes until a prompt window reports non-finite logits. STRATA_NAN_INJECT=1 exercises it.

158, off: 225), down 77 (off: 184); the hashes of the outputs are equal in all three modes.

+# First real `strata bench run` on the released 0.2.1 (terminal 0.2.1, engine 0.1.46 cuda12 Linux packages)
+
+Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS (hand-written run config that mirrors setup: int8 KV, MTP spec 4; z440 layer split auto, P2003 resident experts),
+`strata bench run --profile` (the runner starts and stops the engine), protocol `strata-qwen38-thinking-v1-draft.1`, track `custom`. Dated 2026-10-20.
+
+| | P2003 (RTX 3060 12 GB, Core Ultra 7 265) | z440 (2x RTX A4000, Xeon E5-2643 v3) |
+|---|---|---|
+| `short` decode tok/s (median of 3) | 64.4 | 90.3 |
+| `prompt-4k` prompt / decode tok/s, TTFT | 962 / 55.4, 4.28 s | 1158 / 74.0, 3.56 s |
+| `prompt-16k` prompt / decode tok/s, TTFT | 1103 / 56.1, 14.9 s | 1852 / 75.8, 8.9 s |
+| sanity checks | 12 of 12 | 12 of 12 |
+| required suite after loading | 3 min 12 s | 2 min 24 s |
+| optional concurrency (4 at once, server capacity 1), total tok/s | 54.5, 56.4, 56.5 | 72.3, 69.8, 75.4 |
+
+Numbers are from `run3-with-fixes` on each box (run1 and run2 agree within a few percent). Each box has three runs:
+
+- `run1-release-archive-as-shipped`: the release terminal archive untouched. Status `nonconforming`: the archive has no `COMMIT` file.
+- `run2-with-commit-and-optional-concurrency`: the same plus a `COMMIT` file (the release commit, added by hand) and `--optional-concurrency`. Status `complete`.
+- `run3-with-fixes`: the bench fixes of this branch overlaid on the release terminal. Status `complete`; storage, runtime, engine log and fresh-load line are filled.
+  (The track note says "box: BOX" because the run script was not given the box name.)
+
+## What the protocol and the runner got wrong (fixed on this branch unless marked)
+
+1. The release archive carried no COMMIT, so every release run was nonconforming. `package_terminal.py` takes `--commit` / `STRATA_COMMIT` and refuses to build a distributable archive without one. The release must be rebuilt (or a COMMIT file added) for a conforming result.
+2. The drive of the model files was not found on an LVM volume (`lsblk -s` nests two levels): "Storage: not measured" on z440.
+3. No CUDA runtime on P2003: driver 615 prints `CUDA UMD Version`. Also `nvidia-smi` reports the newest CUDA the driver supports (13.0 / 13.4), not the library the engine ran on (12.9). Now: runtime = the engine's build runtime from `engine-component.json`, plus `cuda-driver-supports`.
+4. `engine.log` in the result was empty (`serve --quiet`). Now the run config's log from the start of the run.
+5. A freshly started engine was reported as "could not tell whether the server was freshly loaded".
+6. The protocol said 20 to 30 minutes after loading, unmeasured. Measured: 2 to 4 minutes (plus 1.5 to 2 minutes for the optional stage and 1.5 to 5 minutes of model hashing before the clock starts). Text corrected in the protocol, COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md, BENCH.bat and bench.sh.
+7. 35 of 36 4K/16K performance requests (and 5 of 18 `short`) stop at the 512-token cap while still reasoning, so "Total s" is the time to the cap and "first answer" is mostly missing. The readouts now carry a `Capped` column and say so. The cap itself is part of the frozen protocol (a change needs a new protocol ID); a larger cap or a non-reasoning performance prompt is the proposal if the owner wants answer times.
+8. The `short` prompt is about 80 tokens, so its prompt rate (130 to 190 tok/s) is the fixed cost of a request, not a speed. The readouts leave it out (results.json keeps it).
+9. Not fixed: the runner hashes the model files while the engine is already loaded (RAM is tight on a 46 GB box with a 44 GB model; it worked) and the hash time is outside `required_duration_s`; run-to-run decode varies up to 9 % between runs with the same engine (adaptive expert cache), more than the protocol's min-max spread within one run shows.
